transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I feel like I’ve lost the drive and interest in everything I used to care about, even my students and the arts stuff I loved. I just don't have the motivation anymore, and it feels like the spark I used to have is completely gone.

Did these changes start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without any clear trigger? Have you had other similar episodes of losing interest or feeling depressed in the past?

It started about 14 months ago during a very stressful school year when they rolled out a new standardized curriculum, which really felt like the trigger. I have never experienced anything like this in the past, as this is the first time I've ever felt so completely drained of my drive.

Since that stressful school year ended or changed, have your low mood and loss of interest improved at all, or have they continued even without the stress being as intense? Also, do these symptoms still feel closely tied to work stress, or do they now feel present most of the time regardless of what is happening?

No, they haven't improved at all, and this empty feeling has actually been building continuously for over a year now. It doesn't feel tied just to work stress anymore because it's present all the time, even when I'm at home and can't bring myself to care about theater or my daily activities.

Over the past two weeks, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? Which of these have been present for you?

I haven't really experienced changes in my sleep or appetite, and I don't have feelings of worthlessness or thoughts of self-harm. However, I do struggle quite a bit with focus, along with that general lack of drive I mentioned.

Along with losing interest and motivation, have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least the past two weeks? Or is it more a sense of emptiness and lack of drive without feeling particularly sad?

It is definitely more of a sense of emptiness and a complete loss of my spark rather than feeling actively sad or depressed. I don't cry or feel deep sadness, but I just feel completely flat, going through the motions and sitting on the couch unable to care enough to start anything.
Before this started 14 months ago, were there at least 2 years when you felt down, empty, or unmotivated most days? Or was your mood and motivation basically normal until this began?

No, my mood and motivation were completely normal before this started 14 months ago. I had always been very active, successfully managing a busy schedule of teaching, coaching, and organizing community theater with plenty of energy and drive. This decline has been a very clear and drastic change from my previous level of functioning.

How much has this loss of interest and motivation affected your day-to-day functioning at work and home? For example, are you still able to keep up with teaching, chores, and basic responsibilities, or are you falling behind?

It's had a huge impact—my teaching evaluations have dropped significantly, and I was nearly put on a performance improvement plan at school. I've had to step back from coaching and theater, and at home, I mostly just sit on the couch ignoring my lesson plans and scripts. It's really straining my relationships with my husband, colleagues, and friends because I just can't keep up anymore.

Have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing something that others say isn’t true? Even when you know you’re not feeling like yourself, has anything like that happened during this period?

Yes, actually... lately when I'm alone in my classroom after school, I've started hearing a male and a female voice saying things like, "She's failing them," even though no one is there. I've also become convinced that the new curriculum was designed specifically to target me and make me look incompetent, though my husband and coworkers keep telling me that's irrational.

When you hear these voices or think the curriculum was designed to target you, do they fit with your feelings of failure and loss of motivation, or do they seem unrelated to your mood? Have you had any other unusual beliefs or experiences outside of this depressive period?

They definitely feel closely tied to my feelings of failure, since the voices literally say "She's failing them" and the curriculum conspiracy feels designed to make me look incompetent, mirroring my internal sense of failing at my job. However, these experiences only started in the last few months, while my loss of drive has been going on for over a year now. I haven't had any other unusual beliefs or experiences outside of these.

This is most consistent with a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.
